A1.justification: Despite retitling and substantial revision, both PDFs describe the same symmetrized-target diffusion work. All 19 pages of v1 and 33 pages of v2, including appendices, provide readable material sufficient to match retained methods, proofs, experiments, and displays.

before.justification: v1 reports original 1D and 2D synthetic experiments and molecular conformer generation results, including evaluations of its loss with ETDiff and ETFlow.

after.justification: v2 reports original synthetic, molecular, crystal, and protein experiments, plus estimator analyses in Appendix D. These include original outcomes beyond the baseline results attributed to earlier work.

M1.justification: The posterior-average target is retained, but the practical procedure changes. v1 Algorithm 1 samples dataset points and uniform group transformations; v2 restricts sampling to the source point's orbit, includes the identity, and introduces noise-dependent proposals with importance-weight corrections. The wrapped-normal translation proposal for crystal models is a substantive additional adaptation, not merely the renaming to Orbit Diffusion.

E1.justification: v2 retains the 1D reflection task and GEOM-QM9 but removes the 2D four-point rotation/permutation experiment. It adds composition-conditioned crystal prediction and short/long text-conditioned crystal generation on Perov-5 and MP-20, plus protein backbone generation using Foldseek AFDB structures. These substantially broaden the represented domains and task requirements.

E2.justification: The retained synthetic comparison gains an augmentation-only EquiNet comparator. Molecular quality comparisons add GeoMol and GeoDiff while removing ETDiff and its modified counterpart. New crystal and protein comparisons include P-cG-SchNet, CDVAE, DiffCSP, TGDMat, PROTEINA, a controlled finetuning baseline, and additional protein generators in Table 9. GeoDiff was previously cited but not included in v1's results table.

E3.justification: Molecular evaluation adds coverage at 0.5 Å alongside the retained 0.1 Å threshold and distinguishes published, checkpoint, and retrained ETFlow conditions. New protocols include one prediction per test crystal with structural matching rules, and 500 protein samples across five lengths evaluated through ProteinMPNN and ESMFold. Protein finetuning also introduces a comparison using the same computational budget.

E4.justification: v2 removes the 2D sampling-step analysis but adds substantial tests of the method's behavior: augmentation controls, uniform versus wrapped-normal proposals, sensitivity to 100–10,000 group samples, gradient-norm variance across noise levels and checkpoints, and protein equivariance errors. Appendix D examines estimation bias using eight conformers. Molecular, crystal, and protein visualizations add qualitative case evidence.

E5.justification: The synthetic table retains mean and standard deviation, but v2 omits v1's explicit three-seed evaluation count. Appendix C.2 newly specifies medians from three crystal evaluations, while Appendix D.2 specifies eight Monte Carlo seeds and averaging over ten noisy inputs per noise level. These change statistical documentation and aggregation without establishing increased runs for retained experiments.

E6.justification: Synthetic scores and their scale factors change, molecular results are revised, and the ETDiff quality rows and 2D toy results disappear. For example, MCF's mean recall AMR changes from 0.092 to 0.103. New crystal, protein, and estimator results include 95.6% protein designability versus 93.8% for finetuning with the same budget. Changed ETFlow provenance and omitted toy settings limit direct performance comparisons between versions.

T1.justification: v2 revises the variance theorem from an equivariant-denoiser comparison to a Rao–Blackwell estimator statement assuming an exact conditional expectation, adding a strictness condition. It adds an orbit-expectation equivariance theorem, proposal-weight derivations, and flow-matching derivations. Group assumptions change from linear isometries to locally compact isometry groups. The forward-symmetrization lemma and non-equivariant counterexample are substantially retained and relocated.

C1.justification: The existing symmetry and variance-reduction contributions are broadened into a framework claimed to improve both augmentation-based and architecturally equivariant training, with strictly lower estimator variance under stated conditions. The abstract and introduction additionally claim state-of-the-art GEOM-QM9 performance and improvements in crystal, text-guided crystal, and protein generation; v1's empirical claims concern synthetic and molecular generation.

C2.justification: v2 explicitly distinguishes the exact estimator from biased orbit-restricted sampling and explains how this trade-off depends on noise. Its new limitations paragraph discusses missing contributions outside the sampled orbit and restrictions on proposal flexibility. It also interprets protein designability–diversity trade-offs and proposal-dependent variance behavior. v1 primarily discusses optimization stability and possible deviations from equivariance without this approximation-bias analysis.

D1.justification: Appendix C adds molecular splits, automorphism/rotation sample counts, sampling-library information, proposal bandwidths, crystal training budgets and hardware, and protein finetuning resources and batch accumulation settings. Baseline checkpoint and reproduction provenance is clarified. Conversely, v1's explicit synthetic MLP widths, activation, learning rate, batch size, and DDIM step count are omitted. Newly disclosed molecular settings do not establish that those settings changed.

R1.justification: v2 substantially expands positioning through crystal and protein literature, including DiffCSP, TGDMat, PROTEINA, FrameFlow, and Genie2. Its discussion emphasizes complementing both architectural equivariance and augmentation-based models. Earlier references such as Birrell's structure-preserving GANs and Puny's frame averaging disappear. Publication updates to retained works, such as the Song and Bose papers, are bibliographic changes rather than new research coverage.

P1.justification: The title, abstract, introduction, background, and method narrative are extensively rewritten around gradient estimation and Rao–Blackwellization. NSD/SD-centered exposition becomes an Orbit Diffusion presentation. Proofs are reorganized, a main-text related-work section and explicit limitations are added, and the appendix gains a contents page and task-specific organization. This exceeds changes attributable solely to added experiments.

P2.justification: Figure 1 is redesigned from a forward-diffusion illustration into an estimation schematic beside pseudocode. Figure 2 gains a third variant and an inset, while the old 2D Figure 3 is removed. Molecular tables gain threshold and provenance structure, and new qualitative and diagnostic displays appear. Appendix Tables 7–8 repeat main-text crystal results, whereas Tables 6 and 9 expand comparator displays.

improvement.justification: v2 substantially strengthens empirical support and reproducibility. It distinguishes exact variance guarantees from practical sampling bias, investigates that distinction in Appendix D, and tests applicability to different forward processes and non-equivariant models with a controlled protein finetuning comparison. Appendix C supplies important missing implementation detail. These gains outweigh the omitted toy settings and molecular superiority wording that is broader than the mixed-provenance results in Table 2 support.
